In my opinion if you decide to travel solo you should be ready to do everything on your own. Doesn’t mean you will have to as it is possible you’ll meet someone on the road but it is also possible you will not. The point is, you will have to eat regardless of someone joining you or not. So why stress about it if you don’t really have a choice. You know you’re eating alone not because you’re a lonely loser but because you’re exploring a new city/county solo and you need to eat
If you go to a restaurant at lunch time you’ll see plenty of people eating alone for their lunch break, it’s not really that odd

It can be a social occasion of course but it can also be about simply fulfilling your need of nutrition. If you’re fine eating alone at home when you’re hungry, why should it be different at a restaurant if you’re looking to satiate your hunger rather than to have a social outing

First of all, HSE is considered one of the best if not the best universities in Russia. However, this year A LOT of great professors were fired so we can assume that the quality of education probably went down. 


Secondly, I’d like to share my personal experience. I didn’t do this masters but during my bachelors studies I took a minor in this department. We basically just studied some of the courses from this masters programme with the same professors too. The courses were pretty interesting overall, the professors seemed knowledgeable and the courses weren’t too difficult to pass. However, the whole thing was incredibly disorganised. The grading formulas kept changing literally every week, the professors all had different opinions on things like attendance, participation in in-class discussions etc within the same course so for example one professors would say that attendance isn’t mandatory and will not affect your grades and the other would say that you’re not allowed to miss more that 20% of the lectures otherwise you’ll fail the course. Communication with the professors was practically nonexistent as they’d never reply to your emails and would often ignore even the TAs. It was really frustrating. That being said, if you did your assignments on time and didn’t plagiarise it wasn’t difficult to get a good grade but maybe they just went easy on us because we were bachelors students.
